messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, a 73-year-old male, was admitted to the Urology ward with a chief complaint of nocturia, frequency, dribbling, and urinary retention since last month. Ultrasound examination revealed left renal mass. Past medical history included diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and ischemic heart disease. The patient stopped cigarette smoking 20 years ago. The lab data reveals that the patient had mild anemia and his blood sugar was 159 mg/dl. Urine analysis showed 10-15 white blood cells in high power field with a negative urine culture. Digital rectal examination showed a nodular (2-3+) and symmetric prostate. The ultrasound examination showed mild bilateral hydroureteronephrosis with an over-distended urinary bladder. The prostatic volume was 25 cc with retained urine of 950 cc. Computer tomography scanning revealed a hypo attenuated mass in the lower pole of the left kidney with arterial and portal enhancement and delay washout in favor of infiltrative process such as RCC close to left psoas muscle. Mild bilateral hydronephrosis due to enlarged prostate was seen. He was subsequently referred to the surgery department of the hospital for nephrectomy. The specimen was referred to the pathology department. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-up:
After surgery, the patient was followed-up for 5 months. No recurrence or metastasis was diagnosed.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was for a left renal mass, imaged as suspected renal cell carcinoma, which led to referral for nephrectomy. The pathology diagnosis is withheld, but the follow-up for recurrence or metastasis fits a malignancy. Renal cell carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm of the kidney, chapter C, category C64. The urinary retention and prostate enlargement are secondary to the nephrectomy-directed admission.

CODE: C64
